text.en: Deba and Deep took their cows out to graze. They did not know how to count, so they made one mark on the wall for each cow that left, and struck out one mark for each cow that came back. Two marks were left, so two cows were missing, and the boys found them in a field.

Welcome to our first chapter, What's in a Name. It begins with a story of two cowherds, Deba and Deep.
They could not count, so for every cow that left the gate they made one mark on the wall.
When the cows came back, they struck out one mark for each cow. If all marks are struck out, every cow is home.
Two marks were left over. That means two cows were still missing, so the boys went and found them.
Matching one mark to one cow like this is the oldest way of counting. Later people made groups of marks to count faster.
Now think about names. Every name is made of letters, and we can count the letters.
The name with the most letters is the longest name. The name with the fewest letters is the shortest name.
In the textbook game, animals make two teams. The animal with the longest name, like elephant, is captain of the first team. The animal with the shortest name, like ox or dog, is captain of the second team.
Elephant has 8 letters and ox has 2 letters, so there is a big difference between them.
Try this at home: write the names of your friends, count the letters in each, and tick the longest and cross the shortest.

problem.en: Hemant has 36 cows and 23 sheep. How can you keep track of them like Deba and Deep?

text.en: Make one mark for every cow, 36 marks in all, and one separate mark for every sheep, 23 marks in all.

why.en: One mark stands for one animal.

text.en: When the animals return, strike out one mark for each animal that enters.

why.en: Matching one to one shows if any animal is missing.

text.en: If no marks are left, all the animals are back.

why.en: Nothing left over means nothing missing.

prompt.en: A friend says the name Mahesh is longer than Karthik. How will you check?

requiredIdeas.en: Count the letters in each name
Mahesh has 6 letters and Karthik has 7, so Karthik is longer
The name with more letters is longer

commonMisconceptions.en: A name that looks wider is longer

points.en: Marking one stroke for each thing is a way to count.
Striking out marks one by one shows if anything is missing.
The longest name has the most letters and the shortest has the fewest.
